(shared-advisor-router/index.mjs:242-246 resolves the bucket from X-Firm-Id via FIRM_BUCKET_MAP, :101 + :358 rewrite to the key against THAT bucket). Two consequences, the second worse than the first: (a) AC2 would have failed while the producer reported rc=0 and 'OK: wrote'; (b) the key carries NO firm segment ON PURPOSE because the bucket IS the firm boundary, so placing it in the shared bucket expresses that boundary in NEITHER bucket nor prefix. OBSERVATION / INERT -- AC1's INSTRUMENT IS STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO THE WRITE TARGET, and this is the transferable half of the bucket defect. AC1 establishes producer-ness from an AST write call; put_object(Bucket=X) is a write call for every value of X, so AC1 passed identically before and after the bucket was corrected. An instrument that proves a write HAPPENS cannot see WHERE it lands. 2.0.0_SA_COO~Z's ruling s.4 predicted exactly this failure mode as the reason AC2 must not collapse into AC6 ('the TO loses its only chance to catch a WRONG-KEY producer before the trigger is built') -- the prediction was correct and the hazard was live, not hypothetical.
